children: Consumer spending on Savlon and Nimyle, the two brands acquired by diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd in the health and hygiene segment, is expected to more than double to cross  ₹2,000 crore in the medium term, driven by product innovation, portfolio expansion and deeper market penetration.

Post their acquisitions, both brands have registered a multi-fold growth under ITC’s ownership and together have crossed  ₹1,000 crore in consumer spends, growing at over 20 per cent annually, according to industry experts.

ITC bought Savlon from Johnson & Johnson in February 2015 and has scaled up the brand nearly nine-fold over the past decade, while Nimyle, from Kolkata-based Arpita Agro Products in June 2018, has grown eight-fold in around seven to eight years since its acquisition.
"We expect the runway ahead to be just as exciting as the distance we've covered," ITC Divisional Chief Executive, Personal Care Products Business, Sameer Satpathy told PTI.
He said acquisitions should be evaluated over a longer period, and that the real test lies in how a company develops a brand through sustained investment, innovation and distribution.
"Savlon has grown nine-fold in just over a decade, and Nimyle has grown eight-fold in nine years — that is not a one-time bump from a good deal; it's a decade of compounding choices," Satpathy added.

Both brands have been built into "differentiated" offerings by leveraging the company's scientific research capabilities, product development expertise, supply chain strengths and extensive distribution network to address evolving consumer needs.

ITC, which aspires to be a leading FMCG brand in the coming years, has amplified the playbook of Nimyle from being a mere floor cleaner brand into adjacent categories, including kitchen surface sprays and fruit and vegetable washes. The brand currently has seven products and around 20 SKUs.
"It's now a volume leader across eastern India, and we have carried that momentum in the south. The ambition is simple: to take Nimyle wherever Indian homes are, and beyond," said Satpathy.
Originally based in West Bengal and built around the natural properties of neem (Azadirachta indica), Nimyle is now certified by GreenPro, an internationally recognised ecolabel.
It has emerged as the volume leader and the most widely penetrated brand across eastern India, according to Cantor.
ITC has since expanded its presence into all four southern states, making the brand available across the country through e-commerce and modern trade channels.

title: ITC expects consumer spending on Savlon, Nimyle to double in medium term
